stories.headline: The largest animal that has ever lived
stories.summary: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever existed. The longest one scientifically measured was 29.9 metres and the heaviest on record weighed 190 tonnes. The International Whaling Commission banned all hunting of the species in 1966.

stories.headline: A kilometre of falling water in the Venezuelan highlands
stories.summary: Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall. It drops 979 metres over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in Canaima National Park, with a single plunge of 807 metres.

stories.headline: The islands that straddle the equator
stories.summary: The Galápagos Islands lie around the equator, about 900 km west of the South American mainland. HMS Beagle reached them on 15 September 1835 with the young naturalist Charles Darwin aboard.

payload.dispatch: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever existed. The longest individual ever scientifically measured was 29.9 metres, and the heaviest on record weighed 190 tonnes; the heart of one stranded animal weighed 180 kilograms, the largest known in any animal. The International Whaling Commission banned all hunting of blue whales in 1986.

evidence.title: Protection
evidence.text: The International Whaling Commission banned all hunting of blue whales in 1966.

evidence.title: Size records
evidence.text: The longest blue whale ever scientifically measured was 29.9 m. The record-holder female, caught in the Southern Ocean in 1947, weighed 190 t. The heart of a stranded North Atlantic blue whale weighed 180 kg, the largest known in any animal.

reveal.explanation: The ban came in 1966, not 1986. The size figures are right: 29.9 metres for the longest measured, 190 tonnes for the heaviest, and a 180 kilogram heart.

sources.excerpt: It is the largest animal known to have ever existed. The longest blue whale ever scientifically measured measured 29.9 m (98 ft). The record-holder female blue whale was caught in the Southern Ocean on 20 March 1947 and was recorded as weighing 190 t. The weight of the heart of a stranded North Atlantic blue whale was 180 kg (400 lb), the largest known in any animal. The International Whaling Commission banned all hunting of blue whales in 1966.

payload.question: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall?
payload.comparison: Horseshoe Falls, the largest of the falls at Niagara, stands about 57 metres high.

reveal.context: Angel Falls drops 979 metres over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, with an uninterrupted plunge of 807 metres. That is roughly seventeen times the height of Horseshoe Falls at Niagara.

sources.excerpt: Angel Falls is a waterfall in Venezuela with a height of 979 metres (3,212 ft) and a plunge of 807 m (2,648 ft). It is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall. The waterfall drops over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in the Canaima National Park.
Horseshoe Falls stands about 57 m (187 ft) high.

clues: A volcanic archipelago straddling the equator, roughly 900 km west of the South American mainland.
A young naturalist arrived here aboard HMS Beagle on 15 September 1835, and what he saw later shaped a famous theory.

reveal.explanation: The Galápagos Islands are located around the equator, 898 km west of the mainland of South America; islands in the chain lie in both hemispheres. HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin aboard, reached the archipelago on 15 September 1835.

sources.excerpt: The Galápagos Islands (0.500°S 90.500°W) are located around the equator, 485 nautical miles (898 km) west of the mainland of South America. Straddling the equator, islands in the chain are located in both the Northern and Southern hemispheres. HMS Beagle reached the Galápagos on 15 September 1835 with the young naturalist Charles Darwin aboard.
